paragraphs.title: Amaziah's Reign, Vengeance, and Victory over Edom

easy.explanation: Amaziah the son of Joash became king of Judah.
easy.q: Who became king of Judah at the beginning of this passage?

answers: He did evil in the sight of the LORD
He did that which was right in the sight of the LORD
The passage says nothing about his conduct
easy.explanation: The KJV says that Amaziah did that which was right in the sight of the LORD.
easy.q: How is Amaziah described concerning his conduct before the LORD?

easy.explanation: Amaziah smote Edom in the valley of salt.
easy.q: Whom did Amaziah defeat in battle?

medium.explanation: The KJV says, “But the children of the murderers he slew not.”
medium.q: What did Amaziah do to the children of the men who had slain his father?

answers: Because it was commanded in the law of Moses
Because they had fled from Edom
medium.explanation: The law taught that children were not to be put to death for their fathers' sins.
medium.q: Why did Amaziah not slay the children of the murderers?

answers: He captured Selah by military force
medium.explanation: The phrase means that Amaziah captured the place by war.
medium.q: What does the phrase “took Selah by war” mean?

answers: He defeated Edom, became king, and punished his father's murderers
He became king, punished his father's murderers, and defeated Edom
He punished his father's murderers, became king, and removed the high places
challenge.explanation: Amaziah became king, punished the murderers after the kingdom was confirmed in his hand, and then defeated Edom.
challenge.q: Which sequence correctly describes Amaziah's actions?

answers: The people still sacrificed and burned incense there
The people stopped worshipping the LORD
challenge.explanation: The KJV says that the people still did sacrifice and burnt incense on the high places.
challenge.q: What does the fact that the high places were not taken away show?

answers: Every member of a criminal's family must be punished
Only the king can be punished
Each person is put to death for his own sin
challenge.explanation: The passage states, “every man shall be put to death for his own sin.”
challenge.q: What legal principle is emphasized in Amaziah's action?

paragraphs.title: The Conflict between Judah and Israel and Amaziah's Defeat

easy.explanation: Amaziah sent messengers to Jehoash king of Israel.
easy.q: To whom did Amaziah send a challenge?

easy.explanation: The two kings looked one another in the face at Beth-shemesh.
easy.q: Where did the armies of Judah and Israel meet?

easy.explanation: Judah was put to the worse before Israel.

answers: The comparison of the thistle and the cedar
The comparison of the vineyard and the olive tree
The comparison of the lion and the lamb
medium.explanation: Jehoash compared Amaziah to a thistle and himself to a cedar.
medium.q: What comparison did Jehoash use to warn Amaziah?

medium.explanation: Amaziah would not hear, and Judah was defeated at Beth-shemesh.
medium.q: What happened because Amaziah would not listen?

answers: Amaziah had become proud because of his victory over Edom
medium.explanation: Jehoash warned that Amaziah's victory had made him proud.
medium.q: What did Jehoash mean when he said, “thine heart hath lifted thee up”?

answers: Amaziah and the kingdom of Judah
challenge.explanation: The thistle represented Amaziah and Judah in contrast with Jehoash and Israel.
challenge.q: What did the thistle represent in Jehoash's comparison?

answers: He broke down part of Jerusalem's wall and took the treasures
challenge.explanation: Jehoash broke down the wall of Jerusalem and took the gold, silver, vessels, and hostages.
challenge.q: What did Jehoash do after defeating Judah?

answers: The comparison, the challenge to war, and the victory over Judah
The challenge to war, the comparison, the defeat and plunder
The plunder, the comparison, and the challenge to war
challenge.explanation: Amaziah issued the challenge, Jehoash answered with the comparison, and Israel then defeated and plundered Judah.
challenge.q: Which sequence correctly describes the events?

paragraphs.title: The End of Amaziah's Reign and the Rise of Azariah

easy.explanation: Amaziah lived fifteen years after Jehoash died.
easy.q: How many years did Amaziah live after the death of Jehoash?
To which city did Amaziah flee?

easy.explanation: The people made Azariah king instead of his father Amaziah.
easy.q: Who was made king instead of Amaziah?

medium.explanation: A conspiracy was made against Amaziah in Jerusalem.
medium.q: What led to the end of Amaziah's reign?

medium.explanation: The KJV says that Azariah was sixteen years old.
medium.q: How old was Azariah when he became king?

answers: He built Elath and restored it to Judah
medium.explanation: Azariah built Elath and restored it to Judah.
medium.q: What did Azariah do after becoming king?

answers: He succeeded his father in the kingship
challenge.explanation: Azariah, Amaziah's son, was made king instead of his father.
challenge.q: What can be learned from the people's making Azariah king?

answers: Amaziah fled from Jerusalem to Lachish, where he was slain
Azariah was born in Lachish and crowned in Jerusalem
Jehoash left Lachish and built Jerusalem
challenge.explanation: Amaziah fled to Lachish, where the conspirators slew him; he was then buried in Jerusalem.
challenge.q: What relationship between Lachish and Jerusalem is described in the passage?

answers: He died at Lachish but was buried at Jerusalem
He died at Jerusalem but was buried in Samaria
He died at Elath but was buried at Beth-shemesh
challenge.explanation: Amaziah was slain at Lachish and buried at Jerusalem with his fathers.
challenge.q: Which detail distinguishes the place of Amaziah's death from the place of his burial?

paragraphs.title: The Reign of Jeroboam Son of Jehoash and the Expansion of Israel

easy.explanation: Jeroboam reigned forty and one years.
easy.q: How long did Jeroboam the son of Jehoash reign over Israel?

answers: He did that which was right in the sight of the LORD
He did that which was evil in the sight of the LORD
easy.explanation: The KJV says that Jeroboam did that which was evil in the sight of the LORD.
easy.q: What did Jeroboam do in the sight of the LORD?

easy.explanation: Zachariah his son reigned in his stead.

answers: From the entering of Hamath unto the sea of the plain
From Elath unto the valley of salt
medium.explanation: Jeroboam restored the coast of Israel from the entering of Hamath unto the sea of the plain.
medium.q: What territory did Jeroboam restore to Israel?

answers: Because Jeroboam removed the sins of Israel
Because the LORD saw the affliction of Israel
medium.explanation: The LORD saw that Israel's affliction was very bitter and that there was no helper.
medium.q: Why did the LORD save Israel, according to the passage?

answers: Israel had no remaining strength or helper
Israel had already expanded its borders
medium.explanation: The phrase describes Israel's desperate condition and lack of assistance.
medium.q: What does “there was not any shut up, nor any left, nor any helper for Israel” mean?

answers: He did evil, yet the LORD saved Israel
He did right, yet he was defeated
He never reigned, yet he expanded the borders
challenge.explanation: Although Jeroboam continued in sin, the LORD saved Israel because of its affliction.
challenge.q: What tension is found in the description of Jeroboam's reign?

answers: Jonah the son of Amittai the prophet
challenge.explanation: The word was spoken by the LORD through Jonah the son of Amittai.
challenge.q: Through whom was the prophecy about restoring Israel's borders spoken?

answers: The LORD had not yet determined to destroy Israel completely
Israel had already ceased to exist
Jeroboam had abolished the kingdom of Israel
challenge.explanation: The LORD had not decreed Israel's complete destruction, so he saved them by Jeroboam.
challenge.q: What does the statement that the LORD would not blot out the name of Israel imply?
